title: Sprint Gatekeeper Digest and Incident Timeline
content:
Sprint Gatekeeper — weekly digest (Mar 9–12, 2026)

Attendees: Marcus Chen (owner), Aditi Raman, Priya Kapoor, Ethan Morales, Sofia Alvarez, on-call: Team-Alpha rotation

Goal: Reconcile this sprint's release train gating decisions, capture the hotfix origins and timeline, and agree on next-step mitigations for recurring canary flakiness. This note collects meeting minutes, decision rationale, and assigned action items.

High-level summary:
- Canary instability observed during two late-night rollout windows (03/07, 03/09). Root cause traced to a combination of a kernel-level memory regression in the serving runtime (RN-2345) + a rare kv-cache eviction path hit for long-context models.
- Two hotfixes shipped: HF-101 (runtime patch, immediate rollback guard) and HF-102 (kv-cache stabilization). HF-101 prevented further memory spikes; HF-102 reduced eviction churn in internal soak tests.
- Decision: Tighten canary gating thresholds for memory percentiles and add a pre-rollout short soak window (10m) for tiered canaries. Rollout policy updated (see action item 3).

Detailed timeline and notes:
- 2026-03-07 23:12 UTC — Canary deploy of v0.9.13 began (train: sprint-35, route: canary-regional-us). Observatory alerted for memory heap growth above 78th percentile relative to baseline.
  - Initial triage: no immediate code path obvious in app-level traces.
  - Linked ticket: RN-2345 created by Priya (heap-regression-investigation).

- 2026-03-08 02:40 UTC — First hotfix HF-101 authored (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-engineering/pull/312). HF-101 introduced a defensive allocator fallback and an emergency rollback trigger if sustained growth > 70% for 5m.
  - HF-101 rolled to canary; memory spikes subsided within 12 minutes.
  - Observation: small latency bump (+24ms p95) attributed to fallback path when triggered.

- 2026-03-09 15:05 UTC — Post-mortem sandbox tests reproduced a rare kv-cache eviction path where large prefix caches caused thrash with the new attention kernel. Root cause logged as RN-2378.
  - HF-102 proposed to add hysteresis to eviction and backoff writes.
  - Soak test (2h) reduced eviction-induced error rate by ~78%.

Decisions made in this meeting:
1) Canary gating thresholds updated (effective immediately):
   - Memory: trigger at 65th percentile sustained for 3m (was 78 pct / 5m).
   - Error-rate: 0.5% absolute increase over baseline for 2m -> abort rollout.
   - Latency: p95 + 40ms over baseline for 5m -> pause and investigate.

2) New pre-rollout soak: small burst canary (2% traffic) + 10 minute soak before conventional canary expansion. If any gating threshold trips, automatically rollback to previous model variant and pin rollout.

3) Rollout orchestration change: add a two-phase rollout where the release conductor injects HF-check hooks (memory-sample & kv-metrics) and the circuit-breaker TTL respects 10m soak windows.

Action items (owners, due dates):
- Marcus: Draft updated rollout playbook language and publish quick-start checklist (due 2026-03-15).
- Priya: Complete RN-2345 root cause writeup and coordinate with runtime-team for a larger allocator redesign (due 2026-03-22).
- Aditi: Implement canary gating config changes in release-configs repo + add automated synthetic traffic probe (PR target 2026-03-13).
- Ethan: Extend observability dashboard to include kv-cache eviction rates and per-model prefix-cache histograms (due 2026-03-19).
- Sofia: Run cross-zone capacity soak for v0.9.13 with HF-102 applied, collect latency/cost impact matrix (start 2026-03-13, report 2026-03-17).
- On-call (Team-Alpha): Add a runbook snippet for emergency rollback via release-conductor CLI (complete 2026-03-11).

Risk register (short):
- Risk: False positives from tighter memory gating could increase rollbacks and delay feature rollouts. Mitigation: short soak + synthetic probes to reduce noise.
- Risk: Latency regressions from allocator fallback. Mitigation: limit fallback to <10% of allocation calls; monitor p95 continuously.
- Risk: Increased operational overhead from new checks. Mitigation: automate gating evaluation and provide a one-click rollback in console.

Notes for product and customer-facing teams:
- No customer-facing incident required (internal recovery). However, customer success should be notified if there is a scheduled rollout window impacted. Marcus to update the release calendar entry and notify GTM if sprint-35 deploys slide into maintenance window.

Follow-ups and next meeting:
- We will run a focused postmortem doc (owner: Priya) with a section on the allocator change decision and a cost/benefit table for implementing a redesigned allocator vs continuing the fallback. Initial draft due 2026-03-18.
- Weekly gatekeeper sync will remain Tuesdays 10:30 PT; next meeting 2026-03-16.

Appendix (quick refs):
- Immediate PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-engineering/pull/312 (HF-101), PR upcoming for HF-102 (author: Priya).
- Tickets: RN-2345, RN-2378, HOT-101.
- Slack thread: #release-control reference above for live signal dumps.

Free-form notes / brainstormed mitigations (raw):
- Consider moving large-context workloads to a separate serving pool with different kv eviction params. Pros: isolation; Cons: fragment capacity, more cost.
- Explore a cheap in-memory sampling layer to detect prefix cache thrash earlier in the pipeline.
- Short-term: escalate to applied-ml to evaluate model-side prefix trimming heuristics.

End of digest.

-- Marcus
